name: Imnah
overview: Imnah was a male member of the tribe of Levi, known primarily as the father of Kore, who served as a gatekeeper. His role is briefly noted in the context of Levitical duties, highlighting his connection to temple service. There are no additional personal details or notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Imnah means 'good fortune,' reflecting a positive connotation. This proper name is not indicated as being given directly by God, but it carries a hopeful or blessed meaning within the Hebrew context.
familyAndRelationships: Imnah is identified as a descendant of Levi, situating him within the Levitical lineage. He is also the father of Kore, who is noted as a gatekeeper, indicating a family involvement in temple responsibilities. Beyond these relationships, Scripture does not provide further family details.
scriptureSignificance: Imnah's significance lies in his connection to the Levitical priestly line through his son Kore, who held the important role of gatekeeper. This association emphasizes the family's service in maintaining the sanctity and order of the temple. Although briefly mentioned, Imnah's lineage contributes to the broader biblical narrative of Levitical duties and worship practices.
